title: Ethiopian Honey Bread
community: Ethiopian celebrations — honey bread for special occasions
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Ethiopian Honey Bread — a rich, golden loaf made with Ethiopian mountain honey, eggs, and butter, fragrant with cardamom and cinnamon. The celebration bread — served at weddings, holidays, and the most important family occasions alongside honey butter.
longDesc: Ethiopian honey bread is the most indulgent of the Ethiopian breads — the mountain honey gives it a distinctive floral sweetness, the eggs and butter enrich it to a brioche-like tenderness, and the cardamom and cinnamon make it unmistakably Ethiopian.
ingredients: // Glaze: 2 tbsp honey + 1 tbsp water, brushed on after baking
steps: Dissolve yeast in warm water with 1 tbsp honey. Rest 10 minutes.
Combine flour, salt, cardamom, and cinnamon.
Add yeast mixture, egg-honey mixture, and butter. Knead 10 minutes.
Shape into a loaf. Place in greased loaf pan.
Bake at 175°C for 30—35 minutes until deep golden.
Brush with honey-water glaze immediately out of the oven.
chefTips: Ethiopian raw honey has a floral complexity that commercial honey lacks — the bread character is different.
The honey glaze creates a glossy, sticky top that caramelises beautifully.
Lower temperature than standard bread — the honey sugars burn at high heat.
commonMistakes: Too high temperature — honey sugars burn.
cookingScience: Honey's fructose content (higher than glucose) makes it more hygroscopic than sucrose — bread made with honey stays moister longer than sugar-sweetened bread. The fructose also browns at lower temperatures than sucrose, which is why honey bread requires a lower baking temperature.
sustainabilityTips: Ethiopian mountain honey — supporting traditional beekeeping communities.
healthBenefits: Raw honey provides enzymes and antioxidants even after baking.
culturalNote: Ethiopian honey bread is the bread of abundance — made when honey is plentiful, when a celebration is happening, when the family has gathered. Its fragrance — cardamom, cinnamon, and honey — is the smell of Ethiopian celebration mornings.
